_doc: The single registry of every recursive-self-improvement loop in SYNAPSE. Reconciles the June 2026 six-line harness (docs/rsi/) with the July 2026 read-only audit (harness/notes/RSI_SURFACE_AUDIT.md). A loop's rung is the highest rung for which EVERY rung below is also proven -- rungs_proven is a contiguous prefix, never a cherry-pick. 'human_ratified' is flipped by a HUMAN only; an agent may propose any rung and flip none above L3.

ladder.L0: EXISTS -- the mechanism is present in code
ladder.L1: HONEST -- its input signal CAN represent failure
ladder.L2: REACHABLE -- a live non-test path constructs and drives it
ladder.L3: CONSUMED -- something reads its output AND a later decision differs
ladder.L4: DURABLE -- the effect survives a real process restart (two-run proof)
ladder.L5: BENEFICIAL -- a task-outcome metric moved, measured before AND after

_ladder_collision_warning: The June harness (docs/rsi/SPEC.md) ALSO used L0-L4 with DIFFERENT semantics: its L2 meant 'survives a real restart' (this ladder's L4) and its L3 meant 'alters a later decision' (this ladder's L3). June closure claims are therefore NOT directly importable. Every june-harness loop below starts at rungs_proven=[] and must be re-derived by Line A. This collision is the single largest reconciliation hazard in the harness.

verification_legend.verified-at-head: re-confirmed against working-tree code at frame_commit during this frame
verification_legend.audit-cited: asserted by RSI_SURFACE_AUDIT.md with a probe; not personally re-run this frame
verification_legend.unverified: carried from a prior effort or memory; Line A must establish it

loops.name: EpochAdapter -- router tier-threshold adaptation
loops.blocker: The reward signal is a constant. _record_metric is declared (self, tier, latency_ms, success: bool = True) at router.py:917 and NOT ONE of its eight call sites passes success -- router.py:285, :448, :515, :554, :584, :706, :742, :819, each passing exactly two positional args (re-verified at HEAD f427320 on 2026-08-01). _try_tier0 additionally hardcodes RoutingResult(success=True) at router.py:537 without consulting the responses it just collected, which can carry success=False. The no_tier_matched fallback at router.py:367-373 never calls _record_metric at all, so genuine routing failures never enter the sample.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: CRITICAL. Success rate is permanently 1.0, which is above HIGH_SUCCESS_THRESHOLD (0.9), so adjust() takes the 'great performance' branch every epoch for every tier. Audit probe P4 drove 300 outcomes and measured a monotonic slide to the 0.10 clamp floor in eight epochs, then flat for the life of the process. Wiring TierThresholds.get() into router.py:523 converts a decorative mechanism into a live one-way ratchet with no persistence, no versioning and no rollback.
loops.reversal_note: adaptation.py:121-126 -- no disk read, no disk write, always starts at epoch_id=0 with thresholds={}. Bounded only by deque(maxlen=100) and the [0.1, 1.0] clamp. De-facto reversal is process restart, which is amnesia rather than rollback.

loops.name: OutcomeTracker -- agent reward signal
loops.blocker: L1 is unassessable because the loop has no caller to assess. The OPERATIVE obstacle is L2: AgentExecutor has zero non-test constructions in the entire main tree -- the only occurrence is inside the module docstring at python/synapse/agent/__init__.py:12 (the docstring spans lines 1-21). Every other construction is in tests/test_agent.py. executor.py:60 reads OutcomeTracker(memory) if memory else None, but the guard is not the reason it is dormant; there is no live executor at all. Downstream consumers (learning.py:120 get_relevant, :140 get_rejections, :170 success_rate) therefore all read an empty history by construction, with success_rate returning a hard 0.0 at learning.py:191-192.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: LOW while inert. Before wiring, decide wire-or-delete: a reward signal that has never recorded a single outcome is either the missing substrate for every other loop, or dead weight that should be removed rather than resurrected. Line C owns that call.
loops.reversal_note: Not applicable while unreachable. Becomes a live question the moment a production AgentExecutor exists.

loops.name: memory evolution (charmander/charmeleon) -- detector and converter
loops.blocker: The detector fires; the converter does not. Both automatic call sites invoke only check_evolution and then log: store.py:530-547 emits 'Memory evolution triggered: ...' and does not convert; scene_memory.py:486-500 runs on a background thread and logs '... Call synapse_evolve_memory to upgrade' and does not convert. The converter evolve_to_charmeleon (evolution.py:217) has exactly one caller in the tree -- handlers_memory.py:263, inside _handle_evolve_memory, reachable only through the explicit synapse_evolve_memory tool and gated behind dry_run which DEFAULTS TO TRUE at handlers_memory.py:252. No automatic path can reach it. No memory.usd artifact exists anywhere outside pytest temp directories.

L1: Detector observes real accumulated memory state rather than a literal; it can report should_evolve False.
L2: Audit probe Q6: 2 check_evolution calls per 25 add() calls on the live default backend, with a jsonl negative control and a moneta zero-arm.
python/synapse/memory/store.py:810 (SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND defaults to jsonl, and is unset on this machine)

loops.danger_if_closed_now: MEDIUM. evolution.py documents itself as SUPERSEDED by the Moneta backend and says 'do not extend it'. Its own stated removal condition -- that SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND defaults to moneta -- has NOT been met, so the deprecated mechanism is live by default. Closing L3 here would deepen investment in a module marked for removal. Line C (convergence) should decide the substrate before this loop is closed.
loops.reversal_note: Conversion writes a durable artifact; there is no documented un-evolve path. CLAUDE.md requires memory evolution to be lossless or aborted, which is a guard, not a rollback.

loops.name: render-farm learning -- handlers_render memory guard
loops.blocker: L2 REACHABLE is unproven, and it is the ONLY thing standing between this loop and the highest rung in the registry. The wiring is present -- handlers_render.py:1572-1578 sets self._render_farm._memory = get_synapse_memory() (the June fix survived; the line moved from :858 as the file grew). But L2 per SPEC requires production artifacts, and there are none: synapse_live_metrics reports session.total_commands 0 and routing.total_requests 0, and no render has run. The mechanism is correct and has never been exercised in production.

L1: record_fix_outcome declares success: bool as a REQUIRED parameter with no default (render_diagnostics.py:315) -- structurally unlike _record_metric's silent success=True.

Both branches are reachable and pass DIFFERENT values: render_farm.py:249 passes success=True on the validation-passed branch; render_farm.py:280 passes success=False on the exhausted-retries branch, commented 'Record failure for learning'. Verified at HEAD 2026-08-01.

loops._eval_note: tests/rsi/eval_line_r_closure.py PASSES at HEAD, but it is a SCRIPT, not a pytest module -- its eval_ prefix matches neither test_*.py nor *_test.py, so pytest collects ZERO tests from it and a pytest-based check reads as absent evidence. Run it directly: `python tests/rsi/eval_line_r_closure.py` -> OVERALL: PASS. It demonstrates, under eval conditions with a real store: in-process record->read-back; reload across 2/2 FRESH processes; and a decision change (warm _warmup_from_memory returns {'pathtracedsamples': 128.0} where a cold store returns {}). Those are this ladder's L3 and L4 PROPERTIES -- deliberately NOT promoted, because rungs are a contiguous prefix (P3) and L2 is unproven. R is the healthiest loop in the registry and still cannot be called closed.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: LOW mechanically -- the signal is honest and the persistence is real. The danger is EPISTEMIC: R is exactly the loop a reviewer is tempted to mark closed on the strength of a passing eval. An eval proves the path works when driven; it does not prove the path is ever driven. Parked boundary retained: tops_render_sequence (the PDG path) is a separate render entry that never hit the guard.
loops.reversal_note: To be established by Line A.

loops.name: section-16 observability -- RecommendationHistory into agent health
loops._surface_note: shared/conductor_advisor.py is the read side of this loop -- it consumes LosslessExecutionBridge.operation_stats(), MOERouter fingerprint counts, and LosslessEvolution's EvolutionIntegrity failure list, and emits Recommendations. shared/evolution.py (LosslessEvolution, markdown->USD, EvolutionIntegrity) is one of those data sources and is a DIFFERENT module from python/synapse/memory/evolution.py, which is loop A3's superseded charmander/charmeleon path. Both were added after the P1 sweep caught them unregistered at frame time.
loops.blocker: L1 HONEST is unproven -- not refuted, simply never checked, by June or by this pass. The June wiring SURVIVES at HEAD: RecommendationHistory is defined at shared/conductor_advisor.py:363, exported at shared/__init__.py:59,:110, and imported by a real non-test caller at python/synapse/panel/agent_health.py:35. Its eval also passes -- tests/test_area4_observability.py, 10 passed at HEAD. What nobody has established is whether the advisor's INPUT can represent failure: it reads bridge operation_stats, router fingerprint counts, and EvolutionIntegrity failures, and at least one of those (router fingerprint counts, see loop F) is known failure-blind. An observability loop fed partly by a failure-blind source can faithfully report health that was never measured.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: MEDIUM, and the reason is new. This loop's recommendations are SURFACED TO A HUMAN in the panel. A loop that displays advice derived from a partly failure-blind signal spends the operator's trust rather than the machine's. Establish L1 by auditing each of the advisor's three inputs separately before promoting.
loops.reversal_note: To be established by Line A.

loops.name: science registry to substrate -- apex verify deposit
loops.blocker: L1 unassessable; the OPERATIVE obstacle is L2 and it is the SAME defect as A2. The seam is fully built -- python/synapse/science/deposit.py exists and is documented as 'the deposit_fn seam', and Registry accepts deposit_fn at registry.py:26 (defaulting to None at :28). But a tree-wide sweep finds the ONLY construction passing a real deposit_fn at deposit.py:58 -- and that line is INSIDE the LedgerDeposit class docstring's 'Usage::' block, not executable code. Verified at HEAD 2026-08-01 by reading deposit.py:50-62. So science verdicts are computed and never deposited: an unclosed benefit edge with no live caller.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: LOW while inert. Note the PATTERN this shares with A2: in both loops the only construction of the live object appears inside a docstring. That is now twice in this registry, which makes it a codebase habit worth naming rather than two coincidences -- a docstring example is not a caller, and a grep that does not distinguish them reports a wired loop that is not wired.
loops.reversal_note: To be established by Line A.

loops.name: router fast-path session promotion
loops._surface_note: shared/constants.py holds FAST_PATHS and FAST_PATH_PROMOTION_THRESHOLD -- the promotion threshold and the CONSTANTS_HASH that stamps session fast paths. Added after the P1 sweep caught it unregistered at frame time.
loops.blocker: Two independent obstacles, and the L1 one is the newly-identified and more serious. (1) L1: promotion is driven by fingerprint FREQUENCY -- MOERouter.route() increments a per-fingerprint counter and auto-promotes at FAST_PATH_PROMOTION_THRESHOLD (default 3), stamped with CONSTANTS_HASH. Frequency cannot represent failure: a fingerprint that fails every single time is promoted identically to one that always succeeds. This loop inherits A1's constant-success blindness at the routing layer. (2) L4: _session_fast_paths is in-memory only and dies with the process. Both claims need Line A confirmation against HEAD -- CLAUDE.md section 2.3 is the doc source, not a verification.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: HIGH if only the persistence half is addressed. Persisting a frequency-promoted fast-path table across restarts would make a failure-blind promotion permanent instead of process-scoped -- strictly worse than today. Fix L1 before L4. This loop is the clearest illustration of why this harness exists.
loops.reversal_note: Process restart clears _session_fast_paths today. CONSTANTS_HASH stamping means keyword-table drift invalidates stamped entries, which is an invalidation mechanism, not a rollback.

loops.name: FORGE build loop -- fix application and validation counters
loops.blocker: L1 CLOSED 2026-08-01 (RL-2 SIGNAL), corrected the same day after a crucible pass. The prior blocker was: orchestrator.py:177 `fixes_applied += 1  # Optimistic`, orchestrator.py:214 `fixes_validated=0,  # Set after verification phase`, and reporter.py:65 RENDERING that hardcoded zero to a human as `Validated: {metrics.fixes_validated}` -- a constant displayed as a measurement. FIRST QUESTION ANSWERED: no verification phase exists in forge/engine. `FORGE.md` Phase 5 ('VERIFY (Re-run)') is a procedure a human or Claude Code follows, not a module -- grep over forge/ found no apply/verify/re-run function and no runnable entry point, confirming the 2026-06-05 CTO finding. The :214 comment's claimed 'verification phase' was therefore a phantom. Taken the HONEST-REPORTING branch rather than fabricating a validator: fixes_validated is now `None` (the 'unvalidated' sentinel) unless real FixOutcome re-run evidence produced a number, reporter.py renders the word `unvalidated` and never a numeral without a measurement, and a displayed 0 now means only 'validation ran and confirmed nothing'. fixes_applied is derived from confirmed-application evidence and no longer increments on classification. CRUCIBLE CORRECTION: the first pass left a SURVIVING MUTANT at its own defect site -- flipping metrics.py:44 back to `fixes_validated: int | None = 0` passed ALL FIFTEEN of the original tests, because not one of them called MetricsTracker.compute_cycle_metrics; they exercised the CycleMetrics dataclass default (schemas.py:420) and the orchestrator above it, never the tracker entry point in between. Four new tests now kill that mutant, proven RED-then-GREEN by flipping the default in both directions. VERDICT UNCHANGED -- E is HONEST, NOT IMPROVING: FORGE applies nothing and validates nothing, and no live non-test path constructs ForgeOrchestrator (process_results has zero callers outside tests/; still no __main__/argparse/console-script). BLOCKED AT L2.

L0: HISTORICAL defect sites, pre-fix line numbers kept as the record of what was found: forge/engine/orchestrator.py:156,:177,:213,:214 / forge/engine/metrics.py:44,:86,:166-167 / forge/engine/reporter.py:65
AT HEAD the same surfaces are forge/engine/orchestrator.py:132 (process_results), forge/engine/metrics.py:38 (compute_cycle_metrics), forge/engine/reporter.py:106 (the Validated row)
L1: forge/engine/schemas.py:326 -- FixOutcome dataclass (scenario_id/applied/validated/detail); schemas.py:420 CycleMetrics.fixes_validated is `int | None = None`, the sentinel for 'no validation ran'

forge/engine/orchestrator.py:229-235 -- process_results(fix_outcomes=...) derives fixes_applied = sum(o.applied), fixes_failed = sum(not o.applied), fixes_validated = count of applied outcomes with a real re-run verdict, else None; the `fixes_applied += 1  # Optimistic` increment is gone and `fixes_validated=0` is gone

forge/engine/reporter.py:64 -- validated_cell() renders UNVALIDATED_LABEL ('unvalidated') for the sentinel; cycle_report (reporter.py:106) and convergence_dashboard (reporter.py:249) both route through it

forge/engine/metrics.py:44 -- compute_cycle_metrics' own fixes_validated default is the sentinel None, NOT 0. This is the defect site the crucible mutated: a `= 0` here re-fabricates a whole-cycle measurement for every caller that omits the argument, and it sits BELOW the orchestrator, so orchestrator-level tests cannot see it
forge/engine/metrics.py:159 -- MetricsTracker.total_fixes_validated excludes null cycles and returns None when no cycle was ever measured (a null is never summed as a zero)

PARTIAL COVERAGE (crucible finding, CLOSED): the sentinel is per-cycle, so one outcome carrying a verdict used to flip the whole cycle into reading as measured. schemas.py:421 fixes_revalidated records the denominator (applied fixes that carried a re-run verdict), schemas.py:454 CycleMetrics.validation_is_partial is True when it is below fixes_applied, and reporter.py:48 partial_validation_note emits a '! PARTIAL: N of M applied fixes re-run (K unvalidated)' box row

tests/test_forge_engine_honest_signal.py -- 26 tests (15 original + 11 from the crucible correction). MUTATION-VERIFIED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS, three mutants, each observed red then green: (1) metrics.py:44 default None -> 0 fails 4 (test_compute_cycle_metrics_omitting_validation_yields_the_sentinel, test_compute_cycle_metrics_unvalidated_cycle_never_renders_a_numeral, test_compute_cycle_metrics_signature_default_is_the_sentinel, test_metrics_source_carries_no_fabricated_validated_default) and 0 of the original 15, reproducing the crucible's survival finding exactly; (2) validation_is_partial forced to False fails 2; (3) restoring the legacy zeroes in cycles.json fails 1

L1 bar met in the 'honest unvalidated' direction: the signal CAN represent failure -- an applied fix whose re-run refutes it (FixOutcome(applied=True, validated=False)) lowers the count, and an all-refuted cycle yields a MEASURED 0 that is distinguishable from the unmeasured sentinel (test_all_reruns_failing_yields_a_measured_zero_not_the_sentinel)

known_limits: UNBOUNDED SELF-ASSERTION (crucible finding, DEFERRED with reasoning): process_results accepts any FixOutcome list and cross-checks none of it. Deferred deliberately -- there is nothing in forge/engine to cross-check against (no apply stage, no re-run stage, no execution surface of any kind), so any check the engine could perform would be another self-assertion in a different costume; the caller writes scenario_id, applied AND validated. What the fix does guarantee is narrower and real: the engine no longer manufactures counts on its OWN authority, and every count is now attributable to a caller who claimed it. Closing this needs a real verifier that re-runs the scenario and reads the result -- the same missing apply/verify stage that blocks L2. Named explicitly in the FixOutcome docstring (schemas.py:348-360) so the type is not mistaken for a verification boundary.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: HIGH at L2+. June called this 'the ONE large build'. The L1 fix removes the fabricated success value but does NOT build an apply/verify stage -- FORGE still cannot improve itself, it can now only report that fact honestly. Driving this loop live (L2) without first building a real apply+re-run stage would compound unvalidated fixes: the exact hazard in the harness-updating-is-not-harness-benefit lens. Benefit without verification is a hazard, not a win.
loops.reversal_note: Counters persist to forge/metrics/cycles.json (append-only list, no schema version). CORRECTED 2026-08-01 (crucible finding): the three historical cycles carried `fixes_validated: 0` and are NOW rewritten to `null`. The earlier text here said they were deliberately left alone as pre-fix records -- that was wrong under the new contract, where a rendered 0 asserts 'a re-run ran and confirmed nothing'. Those rows are hand-authored (they carry `friction_scenarios` / `scenario_results`, fields CycleMetrics has no equivalent of) and all three also record `fixes_applied: 0`, so no fix ever existed to re-run. Left as zeroes they made MetricsTracker.total_fixes_validated report a MEASURED 0 for the whole project -- reproduced on the real file: 0 before, None after. Pinned by test_committed_cycles_json_claims_no_validation_that_never_happened. Corpus/backlog writes are separate and untouched by this change. Full reversal posture still to be established by Line A.

loops.name: convergence -- two-tier Moneta substrate (subtractive)
loops.blocker: Not a dormant loop but the substrate the other loops converge onto, and it is SUBTRACTIVE by design: delete the bespoke append-logs and repoint at Moneta. Moneta is built and importable (moneta_runtime.moneta_available() returns True) but default-OFF -- store.py:810 reads SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND with a jsonl default, and the variable is unset on this machine. A confounder found by the audit: .synapse/config.yaml:17 says memory_backend: 'flat', a DIFFERENT key that the store selector never reads, so it neither selects moneta nor changes the backend and must not be mistaken for configuration.
loops.danger_if_closed_now: MEDIUM. Flipping the backend default relocates every other loop's persistence substrate at once. Sequence it after the L1 fixes, not before, or the signal work lands on a substrate that is about to move.
loops.reversal_note: SYNAPSE_MEMORY_BACKEND is a genuine reversal lever -- flipping it back restores jsonl -- but data written under one backend is not automatically migrated to the other.
